seven_q.Q0_posture: Analytical and comparative; seeks to establish structural isomorphism between two domains
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-025) mapping immunology to soteriology and sanctification
seven_q.Q3_claim: The immune system's self/non-self discrimination and the sanctification process's holy/unholy discrimination solve the same binary classification optimization problem under uncertainty, with symmetric failure modes
seven_q.Q4_support: 10 independent correspondences, ROC curve analysis, bidirectional predictions, swap test, falsification criteria, and scriptural evidence
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Signal Detection Theory, Janeway's Immunobiology, scriptural passages on sanctification and discernment, other ISOs (002, 003, 026, 027)
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Any sanctification model claiming to eliminate both legalism and antinomianism simultaneously (AUC=1.0) is structurally impossible for finite systems; moral classification always involves tradeoffs
seven_q.Q7_kill: Show moral discernment is not a classification problem; break the dual-pathology structure; demonstrate self-teaching without exposure; show memory is unnecessary; break more than 3 of 10 correspondences

graph_summary.one_sentence: ISO-025 establishes a structural isomorphism between immunology and soteriology, showing that both systems solve the same binary classification optimization problem under uncertainty with symmetric failure modes.
